title: Open-set example
intro: An open-set system must do two things at once: recognise the people it knows, and refuse everyone else. This example enrolls three example people in a private, temporary gallery, then shows the system 13 photos - people it knows, people it has never seen, and strangers dressed exactly like an enrolled person - and reports what it decided and whether that was right.

groups.title: Known people, seen again
groups.blurb: The same person, years apart and in different clothes. The right answer is MATCH with the right person.

groups.title: Known person, but no usable face
groups.blurb: Seen from behind or out of focus. Clothes alone are weak evidence, so the safe answer is REVIEW (ask a person), not an automatic MATCH.

groups.title: Strangers (never enrolled)
groups.blurb: Nobody in the gallery is this person. The right answer is UNKNOWN.

groups.title: Strangers in the SAME clothes as an enrolled person
groups.blurb: The hard case of open-set re-identification: low variance between people. A clothes-only matcher is fooled; the face is not. The right answer is UNKNOWN.

cases.story: A white shirt this time. The system must pick person 2, not person 1.

cases.title: Example person 3 again - head blurred
cases.story: The same street photo style, smaller and darker. The clothes match strongly but there is no face to confirm it.

cases.story: So blurry that even the picture quality is a problem.
